You're working in my app "Audio Tabs". Users either upload an audio file or find a song with the built-in YouTube search, and the app turns it into guitar tabs. I want the tab viewer/player, and the audio → AI tab generation flow behind it, to work like Songsterr's AI tab player, while keeping my app's existing look.

<hard_constraints>
- MUST keep the app's current colour palette, fonts, spacing scale and overall visual style. Reuse the existing theme tokens / CSS variables / design constants. NEVER add new colours, fonts or a new design system. Songsterr is the reference for layout and behaviour only, never for colours or branding.
- NEVER copy Songsterr's logo, name, icons, assets or code into the app.
- Only change files involved in tab generation, the tab viewer and the player. NEVER touch auth, billing, deployment/CI config, or unrelated screens.
- Stop and ask me before you: add any dependency, change the database/storage schema, delete or rename any file, or change the existing upload or YouTube search flows.
- Only build what's listed here. No extra features, refactors or abstractions.
</hard_constraints>

<step_1_explore_then_plan>
Before you write any code, read the codebase and report back:
1. The stack, and where the current tab generation pipeline, tab data format and tab viewer live (file paths).
2. Where the theme is defined (palette, fonts) and how components use it.
3. A gap analysis: each feature in <target_behaviour>, marked exists / partial / missing.
4. An implementation plan in ordered steps, listing the files to create or edit for each step, plus any new dependency (with the reason).
Then STOP and wait for my approval. Don't edit any files in this step.
</step_1_explore_then_plan>

<target_behaviour>
Generation flow (Songsterr-style "AI tab from audio"):
- From an uploaded file or a YouTube search result, a "Generate tab" action runs the existing transcription pipeline, shows step-by-step progress (e.g. separating stems → detecting notes → building tab) and opens the result in the viewer.
- Generated tabs are clearly labelled as AI-generated. If the pipeline gives one transcription per stem/instrument, each becomes its own track.
- Failures show a clear error message and a retry button. The app MUST NOT hang silently.

Tab viewer:
- 6-line guitar tab rendered in measures, with measure numbers, time signature and tempo, and the tuning shown at the start (e.g. E A D G B E).
- Rhythm shown under or above the tab (note durations), plus technique marks the data supports: hammer-on, pull-off, slide, bend, palm mute, vibrato.
- Wrapping, continuous layout that resizes with the viewport and works on mobile widths.
- Track selector to switch instruments/stems.

Player:
- Play/pause, plus a playhead cursor that highlights the current note/beat and auto-scrolls the tab to follow playback.
- Click any measure or note to jump playback there.
- Speed control (e.g. 25%–100%) without pitch change if the audio stack supports it.
- A/B loop: select a range of measures and loop it.
- Metronome toggle and count-in toggle.
- Audio source toggle: original audio (uploaded file or YouTube audio) vs synthesized playback of the tab, both kept in sync with the cursor.
- Per-track mute/solo.
- Keyboard shortcuts: space = play/pause, plus keys for loop and speed. List them in a small help tooltip.
</target_behaviour>

<execution_rules>
- After approval, build one plan step at a time. After each step output: ✅ [what was completed] + files changed.
- After each step, run the existing tests/linter/build if they exist, and fix anything you broke before moving on.
- Keep a checklist of the plan steps and update it as you go. Don't stop to summarise or offer next steps while items remain. Only stop when blocked, when a rule above says to ask, or when everything is done.
- If the existing tab data format can't support a feature (e.g. no timing data for cursor sync), explain the gap and propose the smallest change. Don't invent data.
</execution_rules>

<done_when>
- Generating from an uploaded file AND from a YouTube result both end with the tab open in the new viewer.
- Every feature in <target_behaviour> works, or has been flagged to me as blocked with the reason.
- Cursor sync stays aligned with the original audio within about one beat across a full song.
- The viewer and player use only existing theme colours and fonts, and the rest of the app looks unchanged.
- The build passes with no new errors or warnings.
Finish with a short summary: what was built, files changed, anything blocked or left for later.
</done_when>

No files have been changed yet. Here is the step 1 report. I'll wait for your OK before writing any code.

## 1. Stack and where things live

**Stack:** It's a desktop app. A Python FastAPI server (`app/server/`) runs the engine (`src/audio_to_tab/`), and a Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite front end (`app/web/`) is shown in a pywebview window.

- **Generation pipeline**
  - `src/audio_to_tab/pipeline.py` runs `run_pipeline` (load → separate → detect notes → tab → chords → lyrics → PDF). Lead/rhythm-split runs go through `_run_lead_rhythm_stage`.
  - `app/server/jobs.py` runs each job in a background thread. Progress rows come from `src/audio_to_tab/progress_checklist.py`.
  - `app/server/routes_jobs.py` handles `POST /api/jobs` and `GET /api/jobs/{id}`.
  - Front end: `Entry.svelte` (upload, YouTube search, Convert) → `Waiting.svelte` (polls progress) → `Result.svelte`.
- **Tab data format**
  - `TabDocument` → `TabEvent(start)` → `TabNote(start, end, string, fret, pitch)` in `src/audio_to_tab/tab_generate.py`. Times are in seconds.
  - Each run saves a `result.json` with tempo, time signature, tuning, capo, and the detected beat and downbeat times. A real run in `data/ui_runs` has 158 beats and 42 downbeats.
  - Lead/rhythm runs also save `lead_rhythm_notes.json`, which holds technique marks: slide, hammer-on, pull-off, palm mute and harmonic. It never holds bends or vibrato.
- **Tab viewer and player**
  - `app/web/src/lib/screens/Result.svelte` holds the views, part switcher, a playhead on a fixed-size server SVG, click-to-seek, space to play, and auto-scroll.
  - `app/web/src/lib/components/TabPlayer.svelte` is the transport (play/pause, seek bar, time).
  - The SVG is built by `app/server/score.py` using `src/audio_to_tab/notation_view.py` (`tab_staff_svg`, `tab_playhead_layout`). Rhythm stems and beams come from `src/audio_to_tab/tab_rhythm.py`.

## 2. Theme

- Everything is defined in `app/web/src/app.css` under `:root`:
  - **Colours:** `--bg`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--line`, `--text`, `--text-secondary`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--accent-ink`, `--danger`, `--ok`, `--art`
  - **Font sizes and line heights:** `--fs-1…6` / `--lh-1…6`
  - **Spacing:** `--space-1…16`
  - **Corners:** `--radius-1…3`
  - **Fonts:** Satoshi (`--font-ui`, `--font-display`) and JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`)
  - **Motion:** `--motion`
- Components use these through `var(--…)` and `color-mix()` in scoped `<style>` blocks.
- The server SVG has its own ink colours (`#f4f7fb` and `#8fa0b5` in `notation_view.py`). The new viewer will use the CSS variables instead.
- `tests/test_web_tokens.py` checks several of these tokens and some `Result.svelte` details. I'll keep those passing.

## 3. Gap analysis

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Generate from upload or YouTube, then open viewer | **exists** | The button says "Convert". It opens the result when done. |
| Step-by-step progress | **exists** | Rows include Separating stems, Detecting notes and Mapping tablature. |
| AI-generated label | **missing** | |
| One track per stem | **partial** | A Lead / Rhythm / Combined switcher exists, but only for split runs. |
| Error message + retry, never hang silently | **partial** | An error bounces you back to the start with a banner. There's no retry and no warning if progress stalls. One failed poll also counts as a failed job. |
| 6-line tab in measures, with measure numbers | **exists** | It's a fixed-width server image. |
| Time signature and tempo on the tab | **missing** | Tempo only appears in the header line. |
| Tuning at the start | **exists** | |
| Rhythm (note durations) | **exists** | Stems, beams, flags and dots. |
| Technique marks | **partial** | Hammer-on, pull-off, slide and palm mute are saved for lead/rhythm runs but never drawn. Single-guitar runs have none. Bend and vibrato are **blocked**: the pipeline never produces them, and I won't invent them. |
| Wrapping layout that resizes, works on mobile | **missing** | Bars per line is fixed and the image just shrinks. |
| Track selector | **partial** | The part switcher. |
| Play/pause | **exists** | |
| Cursor that highlights the current note and auto-scrolls | **partial** | A line moves and rows scroll into view. There's no note or beat highlight. |
| Click a measure or note to jump | **partial** | Clicking anywhere on the tab works. Clicking a note doesn't. |

| A/B loop | **missing** | |
| Metronome and count-in | **missing** | |
| Original audio vs synthesized tab audio | **missing** | Original and stem audio exist. There's no synth. |
| Per-track mute/solo | **missing** | |
| Keyboard shortcuts + help tooltip | **partial** | Only space. |

**Cursor sync:** notes sit at the times they were detected in the audio, and the cursor follows the audio's own clock, so drift can't build up over a song. Today the bar lines assume one fixed tempo. I'll place them on the beat and downbeat times already saved in `result.json`, so no storage change is needed. The metronome and count-in will click on those detected beats.

## 4. Implementation plan

**No new dependencies.** The synth, metronome and count-in use the browser's built-in audio. Speed uses the audio player's built-in pitch-keeping.

1. **Structured tab data from the server.** `score.py` will also return a `tracks` list next to the current fields:
   - notes, rhythm values and beam groups, reusing `tab_rhythm.py`
   - technique marks from `lead_rhythm_notes.json`
   - measures built from the saved downbeats, or a fixed tempo when none were detected
   - the beat times, time signature, tempo, tuning, and an "AI-generated" flag

   I'll also pass the saved beat grid to `tab_document_for` so the viewer matches the PDF. The Chords, Piano roll and Text views stay as they are.
   - Edit `app/server/score.py`
   - New test `tests/test_score_tracks.py`
2. **Generation flow.**
   - The waiting screen gets a failure state with the message, the hint, **Try again** and **Back**.
   - It will put up with brief connection errors instead of failing the job.
   - It shows a "this is taking longer than usual" note with Retry/Back if progress stops updating.
   - The server gets `POST /api/jobs/{id}/retry`, which reruns with the same audio and settings. The upload and YouTube code itself is untouched.
   - Edit `app/server/jobs.py`, `app/server/routes_jobs.py`, `app/web/src/lib/screens/Waiting.svelte`, `app/web/src/App.svelte` (to pass the retried job id)
   - Add a test to `tests/test_api_jobs.py`
3. **New tab viewer.**
   - Measures wrap with the window width and work on phones.
   - Tuning at the start of each line; time signature and tempo at the start.
   - Measure numbers, rhythm above the tab, and technique marks (h, p, /, P.M.).
   - Track selector, and an "AI-generated" label in the header.
   - The Bars-per-line setting will only affect exports.
   - New `app/web/src/lib/components/TabViewer.svelte`, new `app/web/src/lib/tabModel.ts` + `tabModel.test.ts` (converting between time and measure/beat)
   - Edit `Result.svelte`
4. **Player basics.**
   - Cursor plus highlight on the note being played, and auto-scroll.
   - Click a note or measure to jump there.
   - Speed 25/50/75/100%, kept at the same pitch.
   - A/B loop: shift-click or drag across measures, then toggle the loop.
   - Edit `TabPlayer.svelte`, `Result.svelte`, `tabModel.ts`
5. **Practice audio.**
   - Synthesized playback of the tab using the browser's built-in audio (no library).
   - A switch between original and synth, both following the same cursor.
   - Metronome and count-in on the detected beats.
   - Mute/solo per track.
   - New `app/web/src/lib/synth.ts`
   - Edit `TabPlayer.svelte`, `TabViewer.svelte`
6. **Shortcuts and final checks.**
   - Shortcuts: Space play/pause, L loop, `[` and `]` set A/B at the cursor, − and = speed, M metronome, C count-in, with a small "?" tooltip listing them.
   - Then run svelte-check, vitest, pytest and the front-end build. All are clean right now: 0 type errors, 21 front-end tests and 376 Python tests passing.

## Questions before I start

1. The upload and YouTube screen button says **"Convert"**. Should I rename it to **"Generate tab"**? That touches the upload/YouTube screen, so I'll leave it unless you say yes.
2. Should YouTube search results get their own **"Generate tab"** button? Today you click Use, then Convert. Same reason: off unless you say yes.
3. Technique marks only exist for lead/rhythm-split runs. Should I run the pipeline's existing detection when a single-guitar tab is opened, or only show what was saved?
4. Bends and vibrato can't be shown because the pipeline never detects them. OK to leave those as blocked?
5. Mute/solo will control synth playback. The original recording is one mixed file, so a track can't be removed from it. Is that fine, or should soloing a track in original mode switch to that track's separated audio when it exists?

# Lead vs. Rhythm Guitar: How the Split Is Actually Made

Condensed research brief. Sources marked by type; peer-reviewed work named explicitly.

## Core finding

Lead and rhythm are **functional roles**, not sounds or timbres. Every working system recovers the role from **texture** (single notes vs. chords), **melodic salience**, and **arrangement context**. Production habits (panning, gain, mid boost, delay) correlate with role but don't define it.

In an **isolated guitar stem**, only textural cues survive: simultaneous note count, continuous pitch contour, bends/vibrato, repetition. Foreground-vs-background is a relation to the rest of the band, and isolation destroys it.

## Definitions

- **Common usage:** lead = featured guitar, single-note lines or double-stops; rhythm = accompaniment chords and riffs (Wikipedia, tertiary).
- **Best academic framing** — Régnier, Martin & Bigo (ISMIR 2021, peer-reviewed): two levels.
  - *Textural*: chords vs. single notes.
  - *Relational*: background accompaniment vs. foreground.
  - Rhythm defined operationally as sections that "aim at making the listener perceive the chord progression."
- **Lead-instrument detection** (ICASSP 2025, peer-reviewed): lead = source that "captures the listener's attention with its dominant auditory presence"; guitar solos canonical.
- **Guitar-solo detection** — Pati & Lerch (AES Semantic Audio 2017, peer-reviewed): assumes solo is foreground and "does not usually repeat in a song." Used predominant-pitch + structural-segmentation features.

## Where the binary breaks

| Case | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Two players swapping roles | Keith Richards: he and Brian Jones learned both parts and would "suddenly switch"; "I've always tried to avoid that separation" (Reverb, practitioner). |
| Funk rhythm as the hook | Nile Rodgers: chucking is "structured around the vocal melody"; he plays "the ride cymbal" role (Premier Guitar). Rhythm by texture, lead by salience. |
| One player, both roles | Richards played "nearly all of the lead and rhythm guitar work" on *Beggars Banquet* (Wikipedia). One performer, one tone — kills timbre-based splitting. |
| Classical/fingerstyle | One guitar plays melody + accompaniment simultaneously; duets share timbre. |
| Riff-driven metal | Neural DSP's "Lead" amp is "built for heavy rhythms and solos"; "Rhythm" amp handles leads too (vendor claim via MusicTech). The riff is the hook. |

## Production conventions (correlate, don't define)

- **Panning/double-tracking:** rhythm usually double-tracked hard L/R; lead single and near centre (Apartment Recording; Gearspace). Contested — some engineers pull rhythm toward centre under a solo, others report a centred lead clashing with vocals.
- **Tone:** lead often mid-emphasis, more gain/sustain, delay (MusicRadar: boost 3–4 kHz; "a touch of delay"). But metal scoops mids, and Slash's "Welcome to the Jungle" tone is "predominantly mids" and mostly "bone dry."
- **Roles can be swapped by production:** a mid-boosted, delayed, centred riff reads as lead; a hard-panned, doubled, scooped line reads as rhythm. On "Let's Dance," "the only rhythm is coming from Bob Clearmountain's delays… a complete accident" (Record Collector).
- **Amp sims encode the role in the product:** Archetype: Nolly lists separate Clean/Crunch/Rhythm/Lead amps (vendor docs).
- **No systematic source** on how mix engineers identify roles in inherited sessions; only forum anecdote (track names, soloing tracks, song form). *[uncertain]*

## Commercial tools

- **Moises** (vendor claims): announced lead/rhythm separation Apr 2024, calls it "pioneering." Rhythm = "the foundation… a heartbeat"; lead = "excitement and embellishment." Premium tier; users choose Guitars **or** Acoustic/Electric **or** Lead/Rhythm, not all three. No public paper, model card, training data, or label definition. User report: "Doesn't always work, but most of the time it does."
- **MVSEP**: model 101 "MVSep Lead/Rhythm Guitar," announced Mar 2026 with only a demo link. API lists "Two-stage (SDR 9.21, default)" and "One-stage (SDR 9.02)." **No stated validation set**; no lead/rhythm entry on its public leaderboard. "Two-stage" elsewhere on the site means extract-then-split, so the guitar model probably extracts all guitar first *[inference, undocumented]*. Architecture, data, role definition: undocumented.
- **Smaller tools:** Lacuna.fm admits it separates "roles… rather than… every overdub" (honest: role category, not track). MusiCraft defines lead as "the lead/solo guitar line" and rhythm as "chords and comping." ncosis (open source) just wraps MVSEP.
- **Older workaround:** mid/side processing — "Sum file… more lead, Difference file… more rhythm" (Steinberg forum) — entirely dependent on panning convention.
- **Verdict:** no vendor documents what its models learned. "Lead" is a marketing definition: melodic, embellishing, solo. Quoted SDRs have no comparable test set.

## Academic / open-source

- **Only direct role classifier** — Régnier, Martin & Bigo (ISMIR 2021): 31 high-level features → LSTM, labels each bar rhythm/not. F1 **0.95** on 102 tablatures with manual annotations. **Symbolic only**, small private corpus (MySongBook-derived). Reused as preprocessing in a 2024 generative lead-fingering system (arXiv 2407.09052).
- **Audio solo detection** — Pati & Lerch GSD: 60 rock songs, macro-accuracy **78.6%**, solo precision **63.3%**.
- **Lead-instrument detection** — Ou, Takahashi & Wang (ICASSP 2025): track-wise attention over multitrack MERT. Prior SVM baseline: **26.03% F1 for guitar**. Model trained on MedleyDB lost **32.26% instrument F1** on a live dataset. Lead switches every **23.05 s** live vs. **29.33 s** in MedleyDB → roles change within songs; segment-level labels required.
- **Same-timbre separation** — GuitarDuets (ISMIR 2024): two classical guitars via Demucs; second guitar's SDR "often fell below 1 dB"; model "perceives the second guitar as background noise." Score conditioning gave only "marginal improvement." Glytsos et al.: SDR inflated for monotimbral mixtures; α needed for SDR 5 is **0.8 multi-timbral vs. 0.6 mono-timbral**; criticises GuitarSet comping/soloing pairs because their "distinct role of each guitar" oversimplifies the task.
- **Melody/accompaniment survey** — Rafii et al. (IEEE/ACM TASLP): in single-channel separation "only TF structure may then be used." Cues: repetition (accompaniment), harmonicity + pitch continuity (lead), panning. Built for vocals, transfers conceptually.
- **Datasets:**
  - MedleyDB: stems tagged "whether the stem contains melody" + f0 annotations — nearest audio proxy for a lead label.
  - MoisesDB: guitars grouped as Acoustic / Clean Electric / Distorted Electric, "according to how they physically produce their sound, rather than their role in the mix." Lead labels only for vocals and synths.
  - GuitarSet: "comping" and "soloing" versions per lead sheet.
  - Slakh2100, EGDB, SynthTab, Guitar-TECHS: likely no role fields *[uncertain — transcription/technique datasets]*.
  - DadaGP (26,181 songs) has multiple guitar tracks justified by "two distorted guitars (often one rhythmic and one lead)" — free-text track conventions, not curated labels.
  - Public lead-instrument annotations for MedleyDB v1: `Sonata165/LeadInstrumentDetection`.

## Cue reliability (for an isolated stem)

| Cue | Looks like | Reliability |
|---|---|---|
| Polyphony (single notes vs. chords) | pitches per frame; chord shapes vs. monophonic line | High for textbook rock; fails on double-stop leads, chordal hooks, fingerstyle |
| Chord-progression realisation | bar-level harmonic coverage | High in symbolic (F1 0.95); unproven on audio |
| Continuous predominant pitch contour | stable f0 track, legato glides | Medium: transcription breaks under distortion; riffs have contours too |
| Bends / vibrato / slides | intra-note pitch modulation | Medium: strong lead marker, but rhythm players bend too |
| Non-repetition across song | solo section lacks structural repeat | Medium: needs whole-song context; riff leads repeat |
| Hard-panned doubles vs. centred single | L/R decorrelated vs. centred mono | Medium-low: convention only, contested |
| Mid boost / 3–4 kHz presence | spectral centroid shift | Low: genre-dependent (metal scooped) |
| Gain / sustain / compression | longer decays, flatter envelopes | Low: "Lead" channels used for rhythm |
| Delay / reverb tails | decaying repeats | Low: dry leads exist; delay can create rhythm |
| Foreground salience vs. band | — | **Not recoverable** from a stem |

## Open questions

1. No public audio dataset with **segment-level** lead/rhythm guitar labels, mixed or stemmed. Nearest: symbolic labels (Régnier) and solo-section labels (GSD).
2. No vendor publishes definition, training data, or test set. MVSEP's 9.21 dB SDR isn't comparable to anything; GuitarDuets shows SDR inflates between same-timbre sources.
3. Unmeasured: how much **stereo role information survives** Demucs/RoFormer guitar extraction *[uncertain]*.
4. Untested: whether textural cues that work on tablature transfer to noisy transcriptions of distorted guitar.
5. No systematic literature on engineer identification of roles in inherited sessions.
6. Evaluation unresolved: 2026 arXiv study finds SDR "a poor one for the shape of the attack and envelope" — matters for tab-oriented output.

# Lead vs Rhythm Guitar: What's True, and What the Code Should Do

Standing spec for the audio-to-tab project. Two parts: the evidence (what actually separates lead
from rhythm), and the application (what `src/audio_to_tab/lead_rhythm.py` should change).

If you are an agent reading this: the ground rules in §0 are binding. The cue ranking in §2 is
evidence-ranked — do not reshuffle it. Every number marked **[cal]** is uncalibrated and must be
labelled as such in code.

Evidence tags: **[PR]** peer-reviewed · **[V]** vendor claim · **[X]** practitioner/forum opinion.

---

## 0. Ground rules

1. **Role is recovered from texture first.** Notes-per-attack, pitch-class movement, contour
   behaviour. Timbre, register, gain and delay are tie-breakers and must never be the deciding
   evidence.
2. **Prefer ambiguous over wrong.** A silent `ambiguous` costs nothing. A confidently inverted label
   corrupts the generated tab. This is a product constraint, not a modelling nicety.
3. **No invented thresholds.** Every constant is `CALIBRATED` (has a source) or `UNCALIBRATED` (a
   guess). Uncalibrated constants must surface in the diagnostics so they can be tuned from real
   data.
4. **Out of scope:** a trained two-guitar separator, EQ or panning tricks presented as separation,
   one label per song.
5. **Keep the diagnostics.** A wrong label without a feature trace cannot be debugged.

---

## 1. What "lead" and "rhythm" actually are

Labels for **musical function**, not for a sound.

Régnier, Martin & Bigo (ISMIR 2021, **[PR]**) give the cleanest formulation: the terms operate on two
levels.

- **Textural** — does the guitar play chords or single notes?
- **Relational** — is it accompanying in the background, or foregrounded?

They define rhythm guitar operationally as sections that "aim at making the listener perceive the
chord progression."

That split is the whole problem in one sentence. **Texture survives isolation. Relation does not.**
A guitar stem tells you what was played; it does not tell you what the part was for. Restoring part of
the relational signal is possible only because we still have the full mix (§4, F8).

Corroborating definitions:

- Lead-instrument detection (ICASSP 2025, **[PR]**): lead is the source that "captures the listener's
  attention with its dominant auditory presence."
- Guitar-solo detection (Pati & Lerch 2017, **[PR]**): a solo is foregrounded, and "a solo does not
  usually repeat in a song."

---

## 2. Evidence-ranked cues

| # | Cue | Why it works | Evidence | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Polyphony** (notes sounding at once) | Chords stack; a lead line moves | Régnier 2021 **[PR]**; Foulon, Roy & Pachet 2013 **[PR]** classify bass / solo / chord comping from audio; Lachambre et al. 2009 **[PR]** separate monophony from polyphony using a pitch-confidence indicator's mean and variance over ~1 s | **High** |
| 2 | **Pitch-class change per onset** | Strumming repeats the same pitch classes; a lead line changes chord tone | Inference from #1; cheap and testable | **High** |
| 3 | **Chord-template fit per bar** | Rhythm exists to make the progression audible (Régnier's definition) | **[PR]**, operational | **High** |
| 4 | **Contour continuity + vibrato/bends** | Bends, vibrato, slides, legato are lead vocabulary | Chen, Su & Yang (ISMIR 2015, **[PR]**) detect these from F0 sequences | **Medium-high** |
| 5 | **Melodic salience / pitch-track confidence** | A foregrounded single voice concentrates energy | Pati & Lerch 2017 **[PR]**; Salamon & Gómez salience (IEEE TASLP 2012, **[PR]**) | **Medium** |
| 6 | **Non-repetition across song form** | Solos don't recur; riffs do | Pati & Lerch 2017 **[PR]** | **Medium**, song-level only |
| 7 | **Rhythmic lock to the beat** | Comping patterns align to the grid more rigidly | Inference; weak but cheap | Medium-low |
| 8 | **Panning / doubling layout** | Double-tracked rhythm wide, single lead centred — a convention, contested by engineers **[X]** | Medium-low, only with intact stereo |
| 9 | Mid boost / 3–4 kHz presence / delay | Genre-dependent: metal scoops mids; Slash's leads are dry **[X]** | **Low — do not weight** |
| 10 | Absolute register (median pitch) | Metal riffs sit low; funk chords sit high **[X]** | **Low — down-weight** |
| 11 | Gain / sustain / compression | Amp-sim "Lead" channels are routinely used for riffs (Neural DSP **[V]**) | **Low** |

Read the ranking as: **texture > contour > repetition > stereo layout > timbre.** Any implementation
that inverts this will work on textbook rock and fail on everything else.

---

## 3. Where the binary breaks (design against these)

Each one is a real case, not a hypothetical. They are the reason the system needs an `ambiguous`
outcome rather than a forced binary.

- **Two players swapping roles.** Keith Richards: he and Brian Jones learned both parts and would
  "suddenly switch." Role is fluid *within a song* **[X]**.
- **Funk rhythm as the hook.** Nile Rodgers' chucking is "structured around the vocal melody"; he
  describes playing "the ride cymbal" role. Rhythm by texture, lead by salience **[X]**.
- **One player, both roles.** Richards played "nearly all of the lead and rhythm guitar work" on
  *Beggars Banquet*. One performer, one tone — fatal to any timbre-based split.
- **Classical / fingerstyle.** A single guitar plays melody and accompaniment simultaneously; duets
  share a timbre.
- **Riff-driven metal.** The riff is the hook and the "lead" tone is a rhythm tone.
- **Chordal hooks.** Sarmento et al.'s DadaGP justifies multiple guitar tracks by "two distorted
  guitars (often one rhythmic and one lead)" — a track-naming convention, not a curated label.

Two hard limits to record in the code, so nobody "fixes" them later by adding a bigger model:

- **Same-timbre separation is unsolved.** GuitarDuets (ISMIR 2024, **[PR]**) separated two classical
  guitars with Demucs; the second guitar's SDR "often fell below 1 dB," and the model "perceives the
  second guitar as background noise." Score conditioning gave only marginal improvement.
- **Roles change inside songs.** Ou, Takahashi & Wang (ICASSP 2025, **[PR]**) measure lead changes
  every **23.05 s** live and **29.33 s** in MedleyDB. A whole-song label is wrong by construction.

---

## 4. Current implementation: what to keep, what to fix

Reviewed: `src/audio_to_tab/lead_rhythm.py` (spatial / mid-side / register / HPSS candidates, Basic
Pitch role features, confidence gates, diagnostics JSON).

### Keep

- **HPSS quarantined.** `build_spectral_pair` output is diagnostics-only unless explicitly enabled.
  Harmonic/percussive is not lead/rhythm. Correct, and documented.
- **"Prefer ambiguous over wrong"** as the default emit policy.
- **The pitch-divergence rescue gate.** Raw L/R correlation conflates "mono duplicated into both
  channels" with "two distinct sources panned near centre" — the algebra in the module docstring is
  right, and the fix widens evidence without lowering the separability floor.
- **Diagnostics JSON** with method, correlation, margin and features.

### Fix

| Sev | Location | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| **High** | `RoleFeatures.lead_score` ~L587 | **0.35 weight on median pitch** — the weakest cue in §2. `pitch_n` is normalised from MIDI 50 and saturates by ~80, so most electric content lands at 0 or 1. Reduce to ≤ 0.10 or remove and re-normalise. |
| **High** | `_dominant_pitch_estimate` ~L219 | **Not a predominant-pitch estimate.** One FFT peak over a 4 s window is the loudest partial of a chord; "confidence" is peak/total magnitude, which moves with distortion and level. It will call a power chord "confident monophonic." Replace with per-frame harmonic summation + peak count (§5, F5). |
| **High** | `split_lead_rhythm_guitar` ~L878 | **Zero-margin default to `a_lead`.** When `margin < 1e-9` the evidence is literally tied; emitting `lead` contradicts the module's own guarantee and silently produces inverted labels. Return `ambiguous`. |
| **High** | `split_lead_rhythm_guitar` ~L851–856 | Basic Pitch runs on **raw L and R of the unsplit stem** when there is no pitch evidence. Both channels may contain both guitars, so polyphony and note density describe the sum, not a source. Compute role features on `best.a` / `best.b`, or refuse the split. |
| Med | `extract_role_features` ~L664 | **First + last 90 s only.** Misses a mid-song solo entirely and cannot express a ~23 s role-switch rate. Needs segment-level scoring (§6). |
| Med | `build_spatial_pair` ~L374 | `np.where(|L|>=|R|, L, L-0.5R)` is **not a separation** — it is a distortion. Acceptable only for hard-panned content; flag the output as approximate. |
| Low | `mean_velocity` ~L592 | Basic Pitch velocity is **model confidence, not dynamics**. Contributes 0.05; do not let anyone re-weight it upward. |
| Low | `_mono_to_stereo` on output ~L930 | Discards panning. Fine for a tab app; means emitted files can't be re-analysed by the same stereo logic downstream. |

---

## 5. Feature spec

All computable with what the repo already has: `basic_pitch`, `pretty_midi`, `librosa`, `tempo.py`,
`chords.py`. Prefer **note-list features** — cheap, unit-testable without audio.

**F1 `polyphony_rate`** — median simultaneous notes per onset. Keep as-is; best single cue.
*[cal] lead ≈ 1.0–1.5, rhythm ≈ 2.5–4*

**F2 `pitch_class_change_rate`** — over consecutive onsets, fraction where the pitch-class set differs
from the previous onset's. Strumming repeats `{E,G,B}`; a lead line does not. Cheapest high-value
feature in this list.
*[cal] lead > 0.55, rhythm < 0.35*

**F3 `chord_fit`** — per beat (from `tempo.estimate_tempo_from_audio`), chroma → cosine similarity
against 24 maj/min triad templates, max over templates, averaged over beats. Rhythm tracks the
progression; a single-note lead fits many templates weakly.
*[cal] rhythm > 0.75, lead < 0.6*
Deliberately fails on arpeggios and chordal hooks — those should come out `ambiguous`, not forced.

**F4 `contour_continuity`** — over the top voice: fraction of adjacent note pairs with
`|Δpitch| ≤ 7` semitones and `gap ≤ 120 ms`; plus `vibrato_ratio` = fraction of notes whose
`pitch_bends` have ≥ 2 zero-crossings and std 0.3–2 semitones. Use as **positive evidence for lead**,
never as negative evidence against rhythm — rhythm players bend too.

**F5 `salience_concentration`** — replaces `_dominant_pitch_estimate`. Per frame, harmonic summation
over f0…5f0 across 70–1500 Hz; then `max / sum` and the count of peaks within 10 dB of the max. Lead →
one dominant peak and a low count; chord → several comparable peaks. Median over frames.

**F6 `onset_beat_lock`** — normalised autocorrelation of the onset envelope at the detected beat
period. Comping locks harder. Tie-breaker only. *[cal] rhythm > 0.5, lead < 0.35*

**F7 `stereo_role_layout`** — only if the stem preserved stereo: `side_ratio = RMS(L−R)/RMS(L+R)` plus
inter-channel coherence in 200–2000 Hz. High side + low coherence ⇒ double-tracked rhythm; high mid +
high coherence ⇒ centred lead. Gate on the mix's panning distribution first; a mono source makes this
feature *meaningless*, not "rhythm."

**F8 `foreground_masking`** — the relational cue, recovered from the full mix. For the guitar's
dominant f0 per segment, compute `guitar_band_energy / mix_band_energy` in third-octave bands around
f0 and its first two harmonics. If the guitar owns those bands it is relational foreground,
independent of texture. **Supporting evidence only** — a loud riff also owns its band. This is a
design inference, not a validated result; say so in the docstring.

### Scoring

Replace the two asymmetric weighted sums (`lead_score` / `rhythm_score`) whose weights cite nothing.
Use one feature vector and either:

- a logistic regression fitted on a few hundred labelled segments (preferred — weights become
  evidence), or
- an explicit rubric with each weight annotated by its §2 tier, capped so tiers 9–11 contribute
  ≤ 10% combined.

Either way, emit per-feature values in the diagnostics.

---

## 6. Decision logic

1. **Segment before scoring.** 8-bar windows (fall back to 8 s if tempo fails), hop 4 bars. Score each
   independently. Emit a role timeline, not a song label.
2. **Hysteresis.** Require two consecutive windows to agree before switching. Suppresses flicker and
   matches the observed ~23 s dwell time **[PR]**.
3. **Three outcomes.** `lead` / `rhythm` / `ambiguous`. `ambiguous` is the correct answer for: mono
   source, identical channels, single-guitar arrangements, fingerstyle, chordal hooks, riff-leads. Do
   not backfill it with the prior label.
4. **Separability ≠ role confidence.** Keep them as separate gates, as now. A good split with a tied
   role margin is still `ambiguous`.
5. **Never emit on timbre alone.** If only EQ/gain/panning separates the streams, that's a mix
   difference, not a role difference. Refuse.

---

## 7. Anti-patterns

Each is a documented failure mode, not a style preference.

- Median pitch / register as the primary cue — fails on metal riff-leads and funk chord hooks.
- Gain, delay, mid boost, amp presets as features.
- Assuming hard L/R panning is the norm; raw correlation near 1.0 does not mean identical channels.
- One label per song.
- Trusting SDR between two guitars: inflated for same-timbre sources (GuitarDuets **[PR]**), and a 2026
  arXiv study finds SDR poor for attack/envelope shape — exactly what tab output needs.
- Treating vendor output as ground truth. Moises and MVSEP publish no definition, training data or
  validation set **[V]**; MVSEP's 9.21 dB SDR has no stated test set and so is not comparable to
  anything. MoisesDB itself groups guitars by "how they physically produce their sound, rather than
  their role in the mix."

---

## 8. Evaluation

No public dataset has segment-level lead/rhythm labels in audio. Nearest options:

- **GuitarSet** — `comping` and `soloing` versions. Good for sanity checks; its clean role split makes
  separation look easier than reality **[PR]**.
- **MedleyDB** — stems tagged "contains melody" + f0 annotations. Weak proxy for a lead label.
- **DadaGP** — 26,181 songs, multiple guitar tracks justified by "two distorted guitars (often one
  rhythmic and one lead)." Noisy supervision from track names only.
- **Internal set** — 30–50 segments from the app's own catalogue, labelled by ear. This will beat any
  borrowed dataset for tuning, and it is the only way to measure abstention.

Metrics, in priority order:

1. **Wrong-emit rate** — emitted labels that are wrong. The metric that matters.
2. **Abstention rate** — how often it correctly says `ambiguous`.
3. Per-segment accuracy / macro-F1.

A system that abstains on every two-guitar song is better than one that inverts labels.

---

## 9. How to brief the coding agent

Agents fail here in three predictable ways: they reach for timbre, they invent thresholds and call
them research, and they optimise accuracy when the product needs low wrong-emit. Counter each
explicitly.

### Copy-paste prompt

```text
Audit src/audio_to_tab/lead_rhythm.py against this document.

Ground rules:
- Role is recovered from texture, then pitch-contour behaviour, then repetition, then stereo layout.
  Timbre/register/gain are tie-breakers only and must never be the deciding evidence.
- Do not invent thresholds. Anything not sourced from §2 is [cal] and must be a named constant
  commented as uncalibrated.
- Preserve: confident-mode abstention, HPSS quarantine, diagnostics JSON, "prefer ambiguous over wrong".
- Out of scope: a trained separator, EQ/panning tricks as separation, one label per song.

Stop for review after step 2.
1. Report which §4 findings still hold, with file:line.
2. Propose the minimal diff for the three highest-severity fixes, one test each.

Then implement F2 (pitch_class_change_rate) and F5 (salience_concentration) behind the existing
RoleFeatures interface, with unit tests over synthetic note lists (no audio) and no new dependencies.
Emit both in the diagnostics. Run tests/test_pipeline_guitar.py and the lead/rhythm tests; show output.
```

### Acceptance tests

- Repeated triad stream + moving single-line stream → roles assigned, margin above floor.
- Mono / identical channels → `ambiguous`, no WAVs emitted.
- Hard-panned duplicate of the same material → refused.
- Empty or very short stem → `skipped`, no crash.
- Existing tests green.

### Follow-ups for each failure mode

- **Reaches for timbre** → "Justify each feature by its §2 tier. Tier 9–11 combined may not exceed 10%
  of the score."
- **Invents numbers** → "Mark every constant CALIBRATED or UNCALIBRATED. Uncalibrated constants must
  appear in the diagnostics."
- **Optimises accuracy** → "Order of optimisation: wrong-emit rate, then abstention, then accuracy."

---

## 10. Sources

**Peer-reviewed.** Régnier, Martin & Bigo, ISMIR 2021 (symbolic role classification, F1 0.95, 102
tablatures); Foulon, Roy & Pachet, CMMR 2013 / LNCS 8905 (guitar playing-mode classifier: bass, solo,
chords); Lachambre, André-Obrecht & Pinquier, CBMI 2009 (monophony vs polyphony); Pati & Lerch, AES
Semantic Audio 2017 (solo detection, macro-accuracy 78.6%, solo precision 63.3%); Chen, Su & Yang,
ISMIR 2015 (bend/vibrato/slide from F0 sequences); Ou, Takahashi & Wang, ICASSP 2025 (lead instrument
detection, 23.05 s vs 29.33 s dwell); GuitarDuets, ISMIR 2024 (same-timbre separation); Salamon &
Gómez, IEEE TASLP 2012 (predominant melody salience); Rafii et al. (lead/accompaniment survey:
repetition for accompaniment, harmonicity and continuity for lead); MoisesDB, ISMIR 2023; MedleyDB,
ISMIR 2014; DadaGP, ISMIR 2021.

**Vendor.** Moises newsroom and Help Center (lead/rhythm separation, Premium tier, no published
method); MVSEP model 101 (two-stage SDR 9.21, one-stage 9.02, no stated validation set); Neural DSP

Agent.text:
I checked the older lead/rhythm splitter against your spec. All four serious problems you listed were still there, and I fixed them:

- **Scoring:** it now decides mostly from the playing itself (single notes vs chords, whether the notes change on each attack, how many pitches sound at once). Register, sustain and the transcriber's own confidence count for at most 10% together.
- **Pitch detection:** the old check called a power chord a "confident single note"; it no longer does.
- **When unsure:** a tied score, or two parts that differ only in register or tone, now give "ambiguous" and no separate guitar files, even in best-effort mode. Empty or very short tracks are skipped instead of guessed at.
- **Diagnostics:** every threshold and weight is labelled as not yet tuned to real songs and listed in the diagnostics file.

Your spec's test cases are now automated and pass, along with the rest of the tests, and the project check passes. That includes a strum panned left with a melody panned right, where the melody is correctly picked as lead.

Not done yet:

- The older splitter still judges two long stretches of the song, not 8-bar sections that can switch roles.
- The other proposed measures (chord fit, bends, beat lock, stereo layout, how loud the guitar is in the full mix) aren't built.
- Nothing has been tuned on real songs.

The best next step is to hand-label 30–50 short sections of your own songs as lead, rhythm or unclear, so the error rate can be measured and the numbers tuned.
